title.quote: Implicit Diffusion: Efficient optimization through stochastic sampling
title.value: Implicit Diffusion: Efficient optimization through stochastic sampling

extractions.description: The paper introduces Implicit Diffusion, a single-loop first-order optimization algorithm for optimizing through parameterized stochastic sampling processes (Langevin dynamics, denoising diffusion). It provides theoretical convergence guarantees and experiments on reward training of Langevin processes (Gaussian mixtures) and reward finetuning of denoising diffusion models pretrained on MNIST, CIFAR-10 and LSUN.

type.quote: We provide theoretical and experimental results showcasing the performance of our method.
type.justification: Paper has both theorems and experiments; it mixes both but includes substantial empirical validation.

name.quote: Sampling and automatic differentiation are both ubiquitous in modern machine learning.
name.justification: General ML / optimization through sampling is the core contribution.

name.quote: This approach is inspired by recent advances in bilevel optimization and automatic implicit differentiation
name.justification: The paper connects to and advances bilevel optimization methodology.

name.quote: Sampling from a target distribution is a ubiquitous task at the heart of various methods in machine learning, optimization, and statistics.
name.justification: Sampling methods (Langevin, diffusion) are central.

name.quote: We also apply Implicit Diffusion for reward finetuning of denoising diffusion models pretrained on image datasets.
name.justification: Generative image modeling used as experimental venue.

name.quote: We report results on models pretrained on the image datasets MNIST (LeCun and Cortes, 1998), CIFAR-10 (Krizhevsky, 2009), and LSUN (bedrooms)
name.justification: Image generation is the application venue.
